description: REQ-204's new 'Closed-inventory cross-check' acceptance criterion (behavioral-spec.md lines 521-538) asserts: 'a fresh, full re-read of runtime/loop/prompt.mjs (performed while writing this revision) found that every ranking/imperative phrase discovered across iterations 3 and 4 (FIND-201, FIND-301) falls inside exactly one of the three targets above... or inside the self-labeled... Tips section; none falls outside all of these.' This claim of completeness for the CURRENT file is factually false. A fresh, full read of the ENTIRE current runtime/loop/prompt.mjs (not just buildSystemPrompt, which is all REQ-204/PROP-204a's four-part closed list actually covers) shows buildUserMessage (lines 181-234, a SEPARATE exported function in the SAME file, also part of the system-prompt-adjacent user turn sent to the model every wake) contains its own, pre-existing, un-named steering/ranking mechanism that recommends specific remaining slots and disparages/forbids others based on recent usage: the 'overuse' string (lines 202-203) says 'Do NOT repeat them now. ... Try a path you have NOT tried: [...]. ... Switch to a different earn path. Concretely: deploy idle cash to yield, open or CLOSE an hl trade to realise PnL, or act on what cook already found. Diversify - don't spin one slot.' and the 'avoid' string (lines 205-206) says '... it is FORBIDDEN this wake. Pick a DIFFERENT slot. ... or try a different earn path (hl trade you can close for profit, yield idle cash, a new x402 product). Do something that can realise money.' Both are textbook instances of REQ-203's own prohibited category -- 'any steering text that tells the model WHICH of the remaining options to prefer' -- and neither falls inside any of PROP-204a's three closed targets (the two whole sections, or the two named economy/gig clauses -- all scoped to buildSystemPrompt only), inside the self-labeled '## Tips' section, or inside REQ-204's adjudicated yield-bullet non-target. Crucially, this is not merely my own semantic judgment: 'Do NOT repeat them now' (line 202) is a LITERAL, case-insensitive match for the exact marker 'do not' that PROP-203b's own Tool/Method column names as one of the generic markers a fresh grep must search the FULL file for ('must', 'prefer', 'highest', 'priority', 'first', 'almost never', 'do not', etc.'). A faithful, literal execution of PROP-203b's own specified check -- 'a fresh grep of the FULL file for generic ranking/imperative markers... turns up no hit that falls OUTSIDE the three closed, named targets' -- surfaces this hit today, in the file as it currently stands, proving PROP-204a's closed four-part list is INCOMPLETE for the current file, exactly the failure mode REQ-204's own Gate language says must trigger a spec amendment before either PROP may be marked PASS. This is the third consecutive iteration (after FIND-201 in iteration 3, FIND-301 in iteration 4) in which the 'closed inventory' claimed by the current revision of REQ-204 turns out, on a genuinely fresh full-file read, to have missed a real, currently-present instance of the same defect class -- this time not because of a narrower-than-claimed scope STATEMENT, but because the 'fresh, full re-read' performed while writing this revision (per its own account) evidently never examined buildUserMessage at all, despite verification-architecture.md's PROP-203b explicitly scoping itself to 'the FULL current runtime/loop/prompt.mjs', which unambiguously includes buildUserMessage.
